fixture: Integrator charge-injection bench (issue #102): the full integrator cell + ota_fd clocked for 6 complete phi1/phi2 cycles; the differential and common-mode output step per clock, read in the phi1 hold
result_kind: simulated (ngspice, transistor-level netlists of design/integrator + design/ota/ota_fd; not the behavioural model). SIMULATED, NEVER MEASURED.

conditions.reset: bench-only ideal 1 ohm switches across Ci until 40 ns (cell has none)
conditions.clocks: behavioural rail-to-rail on Vdda from PULSE shape sources, 200 ps edges, >= 4.7 ns non-overlap, no non-overlap generator
conditions.load_per_side: 0.1 pF output parasitics only (integrator 1, case B of design/integrator/SIZING.md)
conditions.spice_options: reltol=1e-5 vntol=1e-7 abstol=1e-13 chgtol=1e-16 (in the deck)

dac.nulled: held at VCM, dn static: the reference branch transfers zero charge while all of its switches still operate and inject
dac.alternating: spec DR-005 references, dn toggled every clock so the ideal transfer cancels over two consecutive clocks

post_v0.note: shipped cell, zero differential input, DAC nulled: the step IS the injection residual

post_v0p1.note: shipped cell, +0.1 V differential input, DAC nulled: signal dependence

post_v0p2.note: shipped cell, +0.2 V differential input, DAC nulled: signal dependence

post_dac.note: shipped cell, zero input, real +/-1.2 V DAC alternating every clock: cross-check that nulling the DAC did not hide an injection term

pre_v0.note: pre-#92 cell (e310b5f), zero differential input, DAC nulled: the #92 baseline

conditions.fs_unit_mapping: model-B ci_offset [FS] = differential output step [V] / 1.2 V, because one x1 unit is (VREFP-VREFN) = 1.2 V of differential output at Cs/Ci = 0.5

corner_set: DR-002 full grid, 5 process x 3 T x 3 Vdda

dac_crosscheck.interpretation: dvod_2clk on the `alternating` variant is NOT an injection residual: it is the finite-gain leak of the +/-0.6 V intermediate state, and it is orders of magnitude above the nulled-DAC bench's noise floor. That is the measured justification for nulling the reference branch -- with the spec references live, injection is unobservable here. Read as a gain measurement instead, it is an independent check of the OTA DC gain against the ~55 dB in design/ota/SIZING.md.

drawn_cap_ratio.note: Area ratio of the drawn sky130_fd_pr__cap_mim_m3_1 devices, not an extracted capacitance: fringe and perimeter terms differ between the two sizes, so the real Cs/Ci is near this but not equal to it. It is here so a capacitor-ratio contribution to the measured slope is visible instead of being attributed to charge injection.

derived.ci_gain_error_caveat: step_slope_v_per_v is the whole input-to-output gain of one charge transfer, so ci_gain_error_bound lumps charge-injection gain error together with incomplete settling and finite DC gain, which sim/integrator-settling and the DC-gain extraction own separately. It is an UPPER BOUND on the charge-injection part, never an attribution of all of it to charge injection. Measured at tt/1.800V/27C while building the bench, three of those mechanisms account for the whole deficit with nothing left for injection: the drawn capacitor ratio (see drawn_cap_ratio), a finite-DC-gain leak whose per-clock droop fits A = 672 against the 667 the independent dac_crosscheck gives, and -- at the slow/cold corners only -- incomplete INPUT sampling, which is a separate mechanism from charge injection and is tracked separately (see README.md "Limits").

sqrt_wl_prediction.note: The sqrt(W L) argument in design/integrator/SIZING.md predicts the differential residual grows as sqrt of the channel-area ratio. `summing_node_switches` is the prediction that applies to the output: only Sti/Str inject into the summing node, and Sbi/Sbr turn-off charge lands on the bottom plate, which the next phi1 re-drives from vinp/rsel before any transfer. `all_phi2_vcm_switches` is SIZING.md's own framing, kept for comparison. Areas are read from the simulated netlists; `nfet_01v8` -> `nfet_01v8_lvt` is part of the #92 delta and changes the charge at equal area, so neither factor is a complete prediction.
